scope: Independent review and strict production replay after guarded PC53 distance was promoted. This is separate from historical diagnostic-only loader experiments; no native expected output or production source was changed by this review.

review.operationOrder: dy = y1 - y0; dx = x0 - x1; yy = dy*dy; xx = dx*dx; square = yy + xx; floor test then ceiling test then sqrt/cap.
reasoning: Original dx FST reload equals the retained dx under PC53 when the subtraction is finite and binary64 normal or exact zero.
A binary64 normal product or sum has the same 53-significand nearest/even rounding as the original PC53 operation; the original extended-exponent implementation handles all excluded exponent cases.
Nonzero operands whose products round to zero fall back explicitly; subnormal products, subtraction outputs, overflow/nonfinite outputs and control words other than027f also fall back.
Nonnegative normal squared terms cannot sum to a new subnormal; an exact zero sum remains exact. Signed input zero is removed by the squares, preserving the original distance result.
Original floor/ceiling/cap loads occur on the same conditional paths for the supported immutable target constants.

Math.sqrt parity is measured on the supported V8/native platform. This finite evidence does not assert mathematical equivalence for every possible JavaScript implementation or nonfinite unsupported Float80 domain.

supplementaryGuardProof.scope: Diagnostic generated guard/property inputs compared to original unchanged JavaScript Float80 helper, supplementary to original-native fixtures; these are not additional native captured calls

productionFrameProof.scope: Retained full original frame after the native-verified initializer and strictly matched prior frames. Expected state/drawing requests are unchanged original hardware observations; this tool reports failures and does not update fixtures.

limitations: This review measures one genuine initialized standard profile through frame1 and supplementary guard boundaries. The final whole-port native replay suite establishes broader regression status; timings are one-process measurements, not a browser frame-rate guarantee.
